    cr.curve_to(-24, 6, -22, 40, -36, 62)
    cr.line_to(36, 62)
    cr.curve_to(22, 40, 24, 6, 10, 0)
    cr.close_path()
    cr.restore()
    solid(cr, P["brass"], finish="metal")
    for wx in (rx - 160, rx + 104):
        _nr_arch(cr, wx, b["base"] - 250, 56, 130)
        solid(cr, (110, 150, 196), finish="glass")
    _nr_arch(cr, rx - 52, b["base"] - 175, 104, 175)
    solid(cr, (112, 70, 44))
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((60, 36, 24)))
    cr.set_line_width(4)
    cr.move_to(rx, b["base"] - 175)
    cr.line_to(rx, b["base"])
    cr.stroke()

    # the churchyard fence along its right side, the gate in it
    GX = 600
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((238, 234, 224)))
    cr.set_line_width(7)
    for fy in (1350, 1400):
        cr.move_to(GX, fy - 30)
        cr.line_to(GX, fy + 20)
    cr.stroke()

    # the congregation in the yard; leavers walk out and line up along the road
    slots = []
    for r_ in range(4):
        for c_ in range(5):
            slots.append((110 + c_ * 92 + (r_ % 2) * 30, 1380 + r_ * 38, 0.9 + 0.04 * r_))
    order = sorted(range(N), key=lambda i: (-slots[i][0] - 0.3 * slots[i][1]))
    NEUTRAL = [(120, 124, 134), (150, 140, 128), (104, 110, 122), (138, 132, 140)]
    SKIN = [(232, 196, 166), (196, 146, 108), (150, 104, 74), (240, 210, 184)]
    GATE = (GX + 70, 1500)

    for j, i in enumerate(order):

        p = prog[j]
        ex = 790 + j * 40
        ey = 1500 + (12 if j % 2 else -6)
        if p <= 0:

        elif p < 0.4:
            q = ease(p / 0.4)
            x, y, s = sx + (GATE[0] - sx) * q, sy + (GATE[1] - sy) * q, ss + (1.0 - ss) * q
        else:
            q = ease((p - 0.4) / 0.6)
            x, y, s = GATE[0] + (ex - GATE[0]) * q, GATE[1] + (ey - GATE[1]) * q, 1.0
        moving = 0 < p < 1

    for y, x, s, coat, ph, mv, sk in sorted(figs):

    if u >= a0 and landed_to >= 1:

    solid(cr, (232, 226, 214))
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((150, 144, 132)))
    cr.set_line_width(3)
    for sl in range(1, 5):
        sx_ = hx0 + lw * sl / 5
        cr.move_to(sx_, 1420 + 30 * math.sin(ang) * sl / 5)
        cr.line_to(sx_, 1492 + 40 * math.sin(ang) * sl / 5)

    # right by the camera: the country lane, cars passing, old gravestones
    cr.rectangle(0, 1600, W, 120)
    solid(cr, (92, 90, 94), edge=False, rim=False)
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((236, 226, 190)))
    cr.set_line_width(6)
    for dxl in range(0, W + 120, 120):
        cr.move_to(dxl, 1662)
        cr.line_to(dxl + 60, 1662)
    cr.stroke()
    for ci, col in enumerate(((176, 44, 40), (52, 92, 150))):
        cx = -380 + ((t * 560 + ci * 950) % 1900)
        _nr_car(cr, cx, 1712, 1.0, col)
    for gx, gy, gs in ((110, 1915, 1.2), (960, 1915, 1.3)):

        cr.arc(gx, gy - h_ + w_ / 2, w_ / 2, math.pi, 2 * math.pi)
        cr.line_to(gx + w_ / 2, gy)

    # Data walks across the yard to the gate, then shoves it wider each

def scene(cr, t, u, pts, host):
    """HERO: three railway handcars racing
    SUBSTANCE: the rolling handcars
    CAUSE: Data cranks the no-religion handcar down the rails, past the Catholic car, chasing the Protestant one
    Three handcars on three rails, each group's share of Americans is how far
    down the line its car gets. Protestants roll out in front, Catholics
    behind them, and Data cranks the no-religion car from the start line
    past the parked Catholic car — its old place stays as a ghost on his
    rail — and pulls up chasing the leader, the gap to it dashed on the
    shot. Landed by 0.62, then held while flags stream and he keeps at it.
    The readout prints only the no-religion share, under a line that names
    no other group, so its number is never read as anyone else's."""
    rows = [(str(l), float(v)) for l, v in pts]

    def val(key, i):
        for l, v in rows:
            if key in l.lower():
                return l, v
        return rows[min(i, len(rows) - 1)]

    lp, vp = val("protest", 0)
    lu, vu = val("unaff", 1)
    lc, vc = val("catholic", 2)
    top = max(vp, vu, vc) or 1.0

    def X(v):
        return 140 + v / top * 760

    pP = seg(u, 0.06, 0.44)
    pC = seg(u, 0.08, 0.40)
    pU = seg(u, 0.10, 0.62)
    xP = 140 + (X(vp) - 140) * ease(pP)
    xC = 140 + (X(vc) - 140) * ease(pC)
    xU = 140 + (X(vu) - 140) * ease(pU)

    landscape(cr, t, "field", horizon=920)
    birds(cr, t, y0=720, n=5, rgb=(50, 50, 60))

    rails = [(1070, 0.9), (1260, 1.15), (1450, 1.5)]
    for y, s in rails:
        _rail(cr, y, s)

    neutral, neutral2 = (150, 152, 158), (122, 126, 134)
    rk = lambda p, ph: 0.28 * math.sin(t * 7 + ph) if 0 < p < 1 else 0.0
    _handcar(cr, xP, 1070, 0.9, neutral2, lp.upper(), t, rk(pP, 0), 1.0)
    _handcar(cr, xC, 1260, 1.15, neutral, lc.upper(), t, rk(pC, 1), 1.0)

    # THE SCALE on the near rail: where the Catholic car stands, as a ghost
    passed = xU > X(vc) + 40
    if passed:
        gs = 1.5
        gx = X(vc)
        cr.rectangle(gx - 85 * gs, 1450 - 36 * gs, 170 * gs, 26 * gs)
        ghost(cr, a=0.85)
        text(cr, f"{lc} {int(round(vc))}%", gx, 1450 + 50, 28, look.INK,
             anchor="center")

    _handcar(cr, xU, 1450, 1.5, P["accent2"], "NO RELIGION", t, rk(pU, 2), 1.0)

    # the gap still to close, dashed from his car to the leader
    if u >= 0.62:
        then_mark(cr, xU + 110, X(vp), 1120, f"{lp} {int(round(vp))}%",
                  a=ease(seg(u, 0.62, 0.66)))

    foreground(cr, "field")
    vignette(cr, a=0.28)

    hx, hy = xU + 22, 1450 - 62 * 1.5
    if u < 0.06:
        host("point", hx, hy, 220)
    elif u < 0.88:
        host("crank", hx, hy, 220, beat=int((u - 0.06) / 0.1))
    else:
        host("cheer", hx, hy, 220)

segments.illustrated_scene:
# scene standard: 2026-10-11.2
def _hb_windows(N, top, base):
    cols = 5
    nrows = max(1, (N + cols - 1) // cols)
    x0, x1 = 172, 668
    y0, y1 = top + 48, base - 58
    gx, gy = 20, 28
    ww = (x1 - x0 - (cols - 1) * gx) / cols
    wh = min(96.0, (y1 - y0 - (nrows - 1) * gy) / nrows)
    out = []
    for i in range(N):
        r, c = divmod(i, cols)
        out.append((x0 + c * (ww + gx), y0 + r * (wh + gy), ww, wh))
    return out


def _hb_times(i, n0, N):
    if i < n0:
        s = 0.06 + i * (0.18 / max(1, n0))
        return s, s + 0.18 / max(1, n0)
    span = 0.38 / max(1, N - n0)
    s = 0.30 + (i - n0) * span
    return s, s + span


def _hb_hurricane(cr, cx, cy, R, t):
    cr.save()
    cr.translate(cx, cy)
    cr.rotate(-t * 0.55)
    for arm in range(3):
        base_a = arm * 2 * math.pi / 3
        cr.new_path()
        for j in range(40):
            r = 34 + (R - 34) * j / 39
            a = base_a + r * 0.022
            px, py = r * math.cos(a), r * math.sin(a) * 0.62
            if j == 0:
                cr.move_to(px, py)
            else:
                cr.line_to(px, py)
        cr.set_line_cap(cairo.LINE_CAP_ROUND)
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((236, 238, 244), 0.85))
        cr.set_line_width(34)
        cr.stroke_preserve()
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((150, 156, 170), 0.6))
        cr.set_line_width(12)
        cr.stroke()
    cr.save()
    cr.scale(1, 0.62)
    cr.arc(0, 0, 30, 0, 2 * math.pi)
    cr.restore()
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((52, 60, 78)))
    cr.fill()
    cr.restore()


def _hb_board(cr, x, y, w, h, a=1.0):
    cr.rectangle(x - 8, y - 8, w + 16, h + 16)
    solid(cr, (206, 168, 112), a=a)
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((150, 112, 70), 0.7 * a))
    cr.set_line_width(3)
    for g in range(3):
        gy = y + (g + 1) * h / 4
        cr.move_to(x - 4, gy)
        cr.curve_to(x + w * 0.3, gy - 4, x + w * 0.7, gy + 4, x + w + 4, gy)
    cr.stroke()
    for nx, ny in ((x - 1, y - 1), (x + w + 1, y - 1), (x - 1, y + h + 1), (x + w + 1, y + h + 1)):
        disc(cr, nx, ny, 5, (90, 92, 100), finish="metal", a=a)


def scene(cr, t, u, pts, host):
    """HERO: a crowded beach house's windows
    SUBSTANCE: plywood storm boards
    CAUSE: Data hammers a plywood board over a window for every major disaster in a year
    A beachfront house on a crowded coast, a hurricane wheeling in over the
    sea. In the 1980s Data boarded three windows a year; the dashed outline
    keeps those three on the wall as the 1980s mark, then he climbs his
    ladder window to window until twenty are boarded, nearly the whole
    house, today's average. Done by 0.68 and held: the storm keeps turning
    and he keeps nailing the last board."""
    rows = by_time([(str(l), float(v)) for l, v in pts])
    (l0, v0), (l1, v1) = rows[0], rows[-1]
    n0 = max(1, int(round(v0)))
    N = max(n0 + 1, min(25, int(round(v1))))
    ratio = v1 / (v0 or 1.0)
    lab0 = l0.split()[0]
    lab1 = l1.split()[0]

    gy = landscape(cr, t, "coast")
    # a storm sky darkening the top of the frame
    g = cairo.LinearGradient(0, 0, 0, 1150)
    g.add_color_stop_rgba(0, 0.16, 0.18, 0.24, 0.75)
    g.add_color_stop_rgba(1, 0.30, 0.33, 0.40, 0.0)
    cr.rectangle(0, 0, W, 1150)
    cr.set_source(g)
    cr.fill()
    _hb_hurricane(cr, 860, 760, 230, t)

    # the crowded coast: neighbours' houses fading into the distance
    for i, (bx, bw, bh) in enumerate([(700, 130, 150), (850, 120, 130), (965, 110, 120)]):
        contact_shadow(cr, bx + bw / 2, 1250, bw + 20, a=0.25)
        building(cr, bx, bx + bw, 1250, bh, [(200, 190, 170), (170, 190, 200), (214, 200, 176)][i],
                 roof_rgb=(96, 102, 114), roof="gable", boards=False)
    haze(cr, 950, 1260, (160, 168, 180), a=0.45)

    # the hero house
    BASE, WALL = 1420, 560
    cast_shadow(cr, 150, 690, BASE, length=320, a=0.3)
    contact_shadow(cr, 420, BASE + 4, 640, a=0.4)
    b = building(cr, 150, 690, BASE, WALL, (226, 214, 190), roof_rgb=(84, 92, 108), roof="gable")
    wins = _hb_windows(N, b["top"], BASE)
    for (x, y, w, h) in wins:
        cr.rectangle(x, y, w, h)
        solid(cr, (46, 58, 76), finish="glass", rim=False)
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((244, 240, 230)))
        cr.set_line_width(6)
        cr.rectangle(x, y, w, h)
        cr.move_to(x + w / 2, y)
        cr.line_to(x + w / 2, y + h)
        cr.stroke()

    # boards: each drops onto its window on the strike
    k = -1
    for i in range(N):
        s, e = _hb_times(i, n0, N)
        if u >= s:
            k = i
        p = ease(seg(u, s + 0.4 * (e - s), e))
        if p <= 0:
            continue
        x, y, w, h = wins[i]
        _hb_board(cr, x, y - 90 * (1 - p), w, h, a=clamp(p * 2))

    s_last, e_last = _hb_times(N - 1, n0, N)
    s_a, e_a = _hb_times(n0 - 1, n0, N)
    early = u >= e_a
    done = u >= e_last

    # THE SCALE on the house: the 1980s' boards stay outlined
    if early:
        xs = [wins[i][0] for i in range(n0)] + [wins[i][0] + wins[i][2] for i in range(n0)]
        ys = [wins[i][1] for i in range(n0)] + [wins[i][1] + wins[i][3] for i in range(n0)]
        ga = ease(seg(u, e_a, e_a + 0.04))
        cr.rectangle(min(xs) - 18, min(ys) - 18, max(xs) - min(xs) + 36, max(ys) - min(ys) + 36)
        ghost(cr, a=0.95 * ga)
        text(cr, lab0, min(xs) - 14, min(ys) - 30, 34, look.INK, face="bold", alpha=ga)

    # right by the camera: a palm bending in the wind, sandbags
    sway = 18 * math.sin(t * 1.3)
    cr.move_to(960, H)
    cr.curve_to(950, 1750, 990 + sway * 0.5, 1560, 1000 + sway, 1440)
    cr.line_to(1030 + sway, 1446)
    cr.curve_to(1020 + sway * 0.5, 1560, 990, 1750, 1010, H)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (130, 98, 66))
    for j in range(6):
        a = -math.pi / 2 + (j - 2.5) * 0.5 + 0.12 * math.sin(t * 1.6 + j)
        tx, ty = 1015 + sway, 1440
        ex, ey = tx + 210 * math.cos(a) + 40, ty + 150 * math.sin(a) + 110
        cr.move_to(tx, ty)
        cr.curve_to(tx + 90 * math.cos(a), ty - 60, ex - 20, ey - 50, ex, ey)
        cr.curve_to(ex - 40, ey - 20, tx + 60 * math.cos(a), ty - 10, tx, ty + 12)
        cr.close_path()
        solid(cr, (64, 128, 72))
    for i in range(3):
        sack(cr, 160 + i * 150, 1700 + (i % 2) * 30, 1.2, label=False)
    foreground(cr, "coast")
    vignette(cr, a=0.3)

    # Data: up his ladder, window to window
    def spot(i):
        x, y, w, h = wins[i]
        return x + w + 62, min(1440.0, y + h / 2 + 150)
    if u < 0.06:
        hx, hy = 800.0, 1450.0
        host("point", hx, hy, 210)
    else:
        kk = max(0, k)
        s, e = _hb_times(kk, n0, N)
        f = clamp((u - s) / max(1e-6, e - s))
        px, py = spot(kk - 1) if kk > 0 else (800.0, 1450.0)
        qx, qy = spot(kk)
        m = ease(seg(f, 0.0, 0.35))
        hx, hy = px + (qx - px) * m, py + (qy - py) * m
        if hy < 1410:
            cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((120, 90, 60)))
            cr.set_line_width(9)
            lx = hx - 24
            cr.move_to(lx - 30, BASE + 10)
            cr.line_to(lx - 30, hy - 40)
            cr.move_to(lx + 30, BASE + 10)
            cr.line_to(lx + 30, hy - 40)
            ry = BASE
            while ry > hy - 30:
                cr.move_to(lx - 30, ry)
                cr.line_to(lx + 30, ry)
                ry -= 46
            cr.stroke()
        if done:
            beat = 100 + int((u - e_last) / 0.09)
        elif kk < n0:
            beat = kk
        else:
            beat = n0 + (kk - n0) // 3
        host("hammer", hx, hy, 210, beat=beat)

    if done:
        fit_readout(cr, f"{int(round(v1))} a year", f"major US disasters · {lab1} · {ratio:.1f}x the {lab0}",
                    80, 520, size=130)
    elif early:
        fit_readout(cr, f"{int(round(v0))} a year", f"major US disasters · the {lab0}",
                    80, 520, size=130)
    else:
        fit_readout(cr, "Major disasters", f"US, the {lab0} to {lab1}",
                    80, 520, a=ease(seg(u, 0.0, 0.05)), size=130)

stories.closing: The record keeps getting broken, year after year.
stories.question: Which country hosts the most refugees?
stories.caption: 123.2 million people are now forcibly displaced worldwide -- a record for the 12th year in a row. The country hosting the most isn't a rich Western nation, it's Iran, and low- and middle-income countries host 73% of the total. Which country would you guess hosts the most? 👇

stories.title: Our Galaxy Is Hiding Millions Of Black Holes

stories.closing: For every black hole we've found, 250,000 more wait, so our galaxy's hidden story has barely begun.
stories.question: How many black holes lurk within 1,000 light-years?
stories.caption: Scientists estimate our galaxy alone might be hiding 100 million black holes -- and we've directly confirmed only about 400 of them. What's your guess for how close the nearest one really is?

stories.closing: Dim your porch light this summer. A darker night is the one thing you can give them.
stories.question: Noticed fewer fireflies where you grew up?

stories.title: Only 30% Of The World Still Drives On The Left
stories.hook: You'd think every road worked the same.
stories.closing: Somewhere, a rental car agency is still confused.
stories.question: Have you ever driven on the 'wrong' side abroad? Tell me how it went.
stories.caption: Only about 30% of the world's population drives on the left -- and it gets even more lopsided once you count roads instead of people: right-hand traffic covers roughly 75% of the world's roadways. Most left-hand countries are old British colonial networks that were simply never worth the cost of switching. Ever driven on the other side abroad?

segments.say: Only about 30 percent of the world's population drives on the left. The other 70 percent, including most of the biggest countries, drives on the right.
It's not 50/50 either. About 163 countries and territories drive on the right, versus 76 on the left -- mostly places once tied to the British Empire.
It's even more lopsided in road miles: right-hand traffic covers about 75 percent of the world's roadways. Left-hand traffic survives mostly on networks never worth the cost of switching.

stories.question: Should everyone use metric?
stories.caption: Only three countries have never officially adopted the metric system: the US, Liberia, and Myanmar -- about 5% of the planet's population. Mixing up units isn't just confusing, it's cost real money and nearly cost real lives: a $327.6 million Mars orbiter in 1999, and a passenger jet that ran out of fuel mid-flight in 1983. Should the US finally switch?

segments.say: Only about one person in twenty lives where metric isn't official: the US, Liberia and Myanmar. So when worlds meet, mistakes happen.

Today, more than half the fish on your plate was raised on a farm.

segments.illustrated_scene:
# scene standard: 2026-10-11
def scene(cr, t, u, pts, host):
    """HERO: a giant gold wedding ring, cracked open
    SUBSTANCE: the crack in the gold band
    CAUSE: Data hammers the cracked ring shut, one strike per year, and the break narrows
    The US divorce rate, drawn as a break in a huge wedding ring standing in
    a field beside a white chapel. The ring is split open on its lower left,
    and the width of the break is the divorce rate. Data stands at the break
    with his sledgehammer. Each year he strikes it, the gold glows hot where
    it lands, and the break closes to that year's rate. The 1990 break stays
    on the ring as a dashed ghost wedge, so one look shows the gap has
    nearly halved. Everything lands by 0.6 and holds there. After that the
    glint keeps moving round the gold and Data keeps working the seam."""
    rows = by_time([(str(l), float(v)) for l, v in pts])
    n = len(rows)
    top = max(v for _, v in rows) or 1.0
    steps = max(1, n - 1)
    a0, a1 = 0.12, 0.6
    span = (a1 - a0) / steps
    k = int(clamp((u - a0) / span, 0, steps - 0.001))
    f = clamp((u - a0 - k * span) / span)
    slide = ease(seg(f, 0.15, 0.7))          # closes on the strike, then holds
    if u < a0 or n < 2:
        val = rows[0][1]
        landed_row = 0
    else:
        v_a = rows[k][1]
        v_b = rows[min(k + 1, n - 1)][1]
        val = v_a + (v_b - v_a) * slide
        landed_row = k + 1 if slide >= 0.999 else k
    keep = sorted({round(i * (n - 1) / max(1, READOUT_SHOWS - 1))
                   for i in range(READOUT_SHOWS)}) if n > READOUT_SHOWS else list(range(n))
    named = max((i for i in keep if i <= landed_row), default=0)
    shown = rows[named]

    CX, CY, RO, RI, SX = 600, 1050, 370, 282, 0.92
    C = math.pi - 0.6                         # the break, lower left, at Data's reach
    GAP0 = 0.75                               # half-angle of the break at the top rate
    gh = GAP0 * val / top
    gh0 = GAP0 * rows[0][1] / top
    GROUND = 1420

    def band(cx, cy, s_, e_):
        cr.save()
        cr.translate(cx, cy)
        cr.scale(SX, 1)
        cr.arc(0, 0, RO, s_, e_)
        cr.arc_negative(0, 0, RI, e_, s_)
        cr.close_path()
        cr.restore()

    def at(r, a):
        return CX + SX * r * math.cos(a), CY + r * math.sin(a)

    # the setting: a field at golden hour, a white chapel behind the ring
    landscape(cr, t, "field")
    b = building(cr, 820, 1030, 1180, 180, (234, 228, 216), roof_rgb=(122, 92, 80))
    sx_ = (b["x0"] + b["x1"]) / 2
    cr.rectangle(sx_ - 6, b["peak"] - 74, 12, 64)
    cr.rectangle(sx_ - 24, b["peak"] - 58, 48, 11)
    solid(cr, (234, 228, 216), rim=False)
    cr.move_to(sx_ - 26, b["base"])
    cr.line_to(sx_ - 26, b["base"] - 80)
    cr.arc(sx_, b["base"] - 80, 26, math.pi, 2 * math.pi)
    cr.line_to(sx_ + 26, b["base"])
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (110, 74, 54), rim=False)
    haze(cr, 700, 1190, (222, 214, 198), a=0.4)
    birds(cr, t, y0=720, n=4, rgb=(60, 56, 64))

    # the ring stands on the grass
    cast_shadow(cr, CX - SX * RO, CX + SX * RO, GROUND, length=340, a=0.3)
    contact_shadow(cr, CX, GROUND + 2, 300, a=0.45)
    band(CX + 28, CY - 16, C + gh, C + 2 * math.pi - gh)        # the band's depth
    solid(cr, (150, 108, 36), finish="metal", rim=False)
    band(CX, CY, C + gh, C + 2 * math.pi - gh)
    solid(cr, (228, 180, 74), finish="metal")
    # an engraved line round the band
    cr.save()
    cr.translate(CX, CY)
    cr.scale(SX, 1)
    cr.arc(0, 0, (RO + RI) / 2, C + gh + 0.05, C + 2 * math.pi - gh - 0.05)
    cr.restore()
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((170, 124, 40), 0.7))
    cr.set_line_width(4)
    cr.stroke()
    # jagged broken ends
    for a, sgn in ((C + gh, 1), (C - gh, -1)):
        for j in range(7):
            r = RI + (RO - RI) * j / 6
            x, y = at(r, a + sgn * (0.035 if j % 2 else 0.0))
            if j == 0:
                cr.move_to(x, y)
            else:
                cr.line_to(x, y)
        edge(cr, (80, 50, 18), width=6)
    # the strike lands: the gold glows hot at both ends of the break
    heat = 0.0 if u < a0 else (1.0 - seg(f, 0.2, 0.75)) * (1.0 if f >= 0.15 else 0.0)
    if u > a1:
        heat = max(heat, 0.5 * (1.0 - seg(((u - a1) / 0.1) % 1.0, 0.2, 0.7)))
    if heat > 0:
        for a in (C + gh, C - gh):
            x, y = at((RO + RI) / 2, a)
            glow(cr, x, y, 110, (255, 150, 50), 0.8 * heat)
            glow(cr, x, y, 45, (255, 236, 180), 0.9 * heat)
    # the diamond on its setting at the top
    dx, dy = CX + 13, CY - RO - 6
    cylinder(cr, dx - 24, dy + 10, 48, 36, (200, 160, 70), finish="metal")
    cr.move_to(dx - 58, dy - 42)
    cr.line_to(dx - 34, dy - 76)
    cr.line_to(dx + 34, dy - 76)
    cr.line_to(dx + 58, dy - 42)
    cr.line_to(dx, dy + 6)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (214, 234, 250), finish="glass")
    cr.move_to(dx - 58, dy - 42)

def scene(cr, t, u, pts, host):
    """HERO: a flowered wedding arch
    SUBSTANCE: the wedding arch itself
    CAUSE: Data shoves the wedding arch further down the garden path, one push per year marriage waits
    The wedding waits longer: the arch at the end of the aisle stands where
    the 1990 median bride (23.9) reached it, and push by push Data shoves it
    down the garden path to where today's bride (28.6) meets it. Distance
    along the path is the age, so the 1990 arch stays as a dashed ghost with
    its year on it and the gap between them is the extra years of waiting.
    Done by 0.56 and held: a just-married car keeps rolling past behind, the
    ribbons blow, and Data gives the arch one more shove now and then."""
    rows = by_time([(str(l), float(v)) for l, v in pts])
    n = len(rows)
    steps = max(1, n - 1)
    a0, a1 = 0.08, 0.56
    span = (a1 - a0) / steps
    k = int(clamp((u - a0) / span, 0, steps - 0.001))
    f = clamp((u - a0 - k * span) / span)
    slide = ease(seg(f, 0.1, 0.8))
    lo, hi = rows[0][1], rows[-1][1]
    if u < a0 or n < 2:
        age = lo
        reached = 0
    else:
        age = rows[k][1] + (rows[k + 1][1] - rows[k][1]) * slide
        reached = k + 1 if slide >= 0.999 else k
    keep = sorted({round(i * (n - 1) / max(1, READOUT_SHOWS - 1))
                   for i in range(READOUT_SHOWS)}) if n > READOUT_SHOWS else list(range(n))
    named = max((i for i in keep if i <= reached), default=0)
    shown = rows[named]

    def ax(v):

    BASE = 1450
    cx = ax(age)

        cr.restore()

    # THE SCALE on the path: the 1990 arch as a ghost where it stood
    if u >= a0 and cx - ax(lo) > 30:

# scene standard: 2026-10-11
def scene(cr, t, u, pts, host):
    """HERO: a giant hourglass with two wedding rings
    SUBSTANCE: golden sand
    CAUSE: Data pours buckets of sand into the hourglass and its lower glass fills to the age brides now marry at
    The closing, as one picture: waiting longer is time running through a
    giant hourglass in the wedding field at sunset. The lower glass fills
    to the women's median age at first marriage, pour by pour from 1990's
    level up to 2024's, so the glass ends close to full. A pair of
    interlocked wedding rings rests on top of the sand and rises with it,
    still whole. That is the second half of the line: later weddings,
    fewer breakups. 1990's level stays marked on the glass with its year,
    so the extra years show at a glance. Everything lands by 0.56 and then
    holds. Data keeps pouring, the sand keeps running through the neck,
    and the birds keep crossing."""
    rows = by_time([(str(l), float(v)) for l, v in pts])
    n = len(rows)
    m = max(1, n - 1)
    a0, a1 = 0.12, 0.56
    span = (a1 - a0) / m
    k = int(clamp((u - a0) / span, 0, m - 0.001))
    f = clamp((u - a0 - k * span) / span)
    slide = ease(seg(f, 0.15, 0.75))
    i0, i1 = min(k, n - 1), min(k + 1, n - 1)
    if u < a0:
        val = rows[0][1]
        landed_to = 0
    else:
        val = rows[i0][1] + (rows[i1][1] - rows[i0][1]) * slide
        landed_to = i1 if slide >= 0.999 else i0
    keep = sorted({round(i * (n - 1) / max(1, READOUT_SHOWS - 1))
                   for i in range(READOUT_SHOWS)}) if n > READOUT_SHOWS else list(range(n))
    named = max((i for i in keep if i <= landed_to), default=0)
    lab, shown_v = rows[named]
    done = landed_to == n - 1

    CX, R, NK = 640, 200, 16
    GT, NECK, GB = 720, 1060, 1400
    lo, hi = rows[0][1] - 2.0, rows[-1][1] + 1.0

    def Y(a):
        return GB - (a - lo) / max(0.1, hi - lo) * (GB - NECK - 30)

    def glass():
        cr.move_to(CX - 0.8 * R, GT)

        cr.curve_to(CX - R, 980, CX - NK, 1010, CX - NK, NECK)

        cr.curve_to(CX - R, 1300, CX - R, 1380, CX - 0.8 * R, GB)
        cr.line_to(CX + 0.8 * R, GB)
        cr.curve_to(CX + R, 1380, CX + R, 1300, CX + R, 1240)
        cr.curve_to(CX + R, 1140, CX + NK, 1110, CX + NK, NECK)
        cr.curve_to(CX + NK, 1010, CX + R, 980, CX + R, 880)
        cr.curve_to(CX + R, 820, CX + R, GT + 20, CX + 0.8 * R, GT)
        cr.close_path()

    WOOD = (128, 86, 52)
    GOLD = (226, 178, 62)

    if done:
        then_mark(cr, CX - R + 10, CX + R - 10, Y(rows[-1][1]), rows[-1][0])

        cr.line_to(lx - 18, 690)
        cr.line_to(lx + 12, 1440)

    # Data: climbs up, then pours bucket after bucket into the funnel

segments.say: Nearly all freshwater is locked up, with 68.7 percent frozen in glaciers and ice caps.
segments.illustrated_scene:
def scene(cr, t, u, pts, host):
    """HERO: a giant glass of Earth's freshwater
    SUBSTANCE: chunks of glacier ice
    CAUSE: Data tosses ice chunks into the glass, one throw at a time, until ice fills most of it
    All of Earth's freshwater is one tall glass standing on the ice field.
    The liquid part (groundwater plus surface water) sits blue at the bottom
    at its true share. Data tosses ice into the glass, throw by throw, until
    the frozen share fills its real 68.7% of the glass up to the brim. That
    lands by 0.56 and holds. After that Data keeps throwing, and the extra
    chunks bounce off the full brim and tumble down onto the snow. The scale
    is the glass itself: brim to base is all the freshwater there is, and a
    dashed mark shows where the liquid ends."""
    rows = [(str(l), float(v)) for l, v in pts]
    tot = sum(v for _, v in rows) or 1.0
    lab, vice = max(rows, key=lambda r: r[1])
    share = vice / tot

    n = 6
    a0, a1 = 0.08, 0.56
    span = (a1 - a0) / n
    k = int(clamp((u - a0) / span, 0, n - 0.001))
    f = clamp((u - a0 - k * span) / span)
    fly = seg(f, 0.0, 0.4)
    grow = ease(seg(f, 0.35, 0.7))
    step = 0.0 if u < a0 else (k + grow) / n
    done = u >= a0 and k == n - 1 and grow >= 0.999

    # the setting: an ice field under a low sun
    gy = landscape(cr, t, "snow")
    birds(cr, t, y0=760, n=3, rgb=(60, 66, 80))

    GX0, GX1, BASE, TOP = 300, 780, 1440, 640
    WALL = 14
    IX0, IX1, IB, IT = GX0 + WALL, GX1 - WALL, BASE - WALL, TOP + 10
    hin = IB - IT
    water_h = hin * (1 - share)
    yw = IB - water_h

    cast_shadow(cr, GX0, GX1, BASE, length=340, a=0.3)
    contact_shadow(cr, (GX0 + GX1) / 2, BASE + 4, GX1 - GX0 + 80, a=0.4)

    # the contents, clipped to the inside of the glass
    cr.save()
    cr.rectangle(IX0, IT, IX1 - IX0, IB - IT)
    cr.clip()
    vgrad(cr, [(0, (196, 214, 228)), (1, (170, 190, 208))], IT, IB, IX0, IX1)
    # the liquid share: blue water at the bottom
    vgrad(cr, [(0, (86, 156, 214)), (1, (34, 84, 150))], yw, IB, IX0, IX1)
    wave = 6 * math.sin(t * 2.2)
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((210, 236, 252), 0.8))
    cr.set_line_width(5)
    cr.move_to(IX0, yw + wave)
    cr.curve_to(IX0 + 150, yw - wave, IX1 - 150, yw + wave, IX1, yw - wave)
    cr.stroke()
    # the frozen share: ice chunks packed up from the waterline
    cols, rh = 5, 64
    cw = (IX1 - IX0) / cols
    nrows = int(math.ceil(share * hin / rh))
    total = cols * nrows
    shown = int(total * step + 0.5)
    ice = (206, 232, 246)
    for i in range(shown):
        r_, c = divmod(i, cols)
        bx = IX0 + c * cw + 3 + (r_ % 2) * 8
        by = yw - r_ * rh
        box(cr, bx, by, cw - 18, rh - 8, ice, depth=12, finish="ice")
    cr.restore()

    # the glass itself, over its contents
    cr.rectangle(GX0, TOP, GX1 - GX0, BASE - TOP)
    cr.rectangle(IX0, IT, IX1 - IX0, IB - IT)
    cr.set_fill_rule(cairo.FILL_RULE_EVEN_ODD)
    solid(cr, (200, 226, 240), finish="glass", a=0.55)
    cr.set_fill_rule(cairo.FILL_RULE_WINDING)
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((255, 255, 255), 0.35))
    cr.rectangle(GX0 + 30, TOP + 30, 22, BASE - TOP - 80)
    cr.fill()
    cr.rectangle(GX0, TOP, GX1 - GX0, BASE - TOP)
    edge(cr, (40, 52, 66))
    # the scale on the glass: brim is all freshwater, the liquid's top marked
    if step > 0.02:
        then_mark(cr, GX0 - 10, GX1 + 10, yw, "liquid", a=ease(seg(u, a0, a0 + 0.05)))

    # Data walks in along the right of the glass as he throws
    walk_in = ease(seg(u, a0, a1))
    hx = 1000 - 160 * walk_in
    hy = 1452

    # the chunk in flight, from his hands into the glass
    if u >= a0 and u < a1 + 0.01 and 0 < fly < 1:
        r_, c = divmod(min(shown, total - 1), cols)
        sx, sy = hx - 30, hy - 200
        ex, ey = IX0 + c * cw + cw / 2, yw - r_ * rh - 40
        bx = sx + (ex - sx) * fly
        by = sy + (ey - sy) * fly - 300 * math.sin(math.pi * fly)
        cr.save()
        cr.translate(bx, by)
        cr.rotate(fly * 5)
        cr.rectangle(-40, -30, 80, 60)
        solid(cr, ice, finish="ice")
        cr.restore()

    # after it lands: he keeps throwing, the extra ice bounces off the brim
    j = 0
    if u > a1:
        per = 0.14
        j = int((u - a1) / per)
        ph = ((u - a1) % per) / per
        sx, sy = hx - 30, hy - 200
        if ph < 0.5:
            q = ph / 0.5
            bx = sx + (GX1 - 60 - sx) * q
            by = sy + (TOP - 20 - sy) * q - 260 * math.sin(math.pi * q)
        else:
            q = (ph - 0.5) / 0.5
            bx = GX1 - 60 + 90 * q
            by = TOP - 20 + (BASE - 30 - TOP + 20) * q * q
        cr.save()
        cr.translate(bx, by)
        cr.rotate(ph * 7)
        cr.rectangle(-36, -28, 72, 56)
        solid(cr, ice, finish="ice")
        cr.restore()

    # right by the camera: broken ice on the snow
    for i in range(4):
        box(cr, 70 + i * 260, 1700 + (i % 2) * 60, 120 + 20 * (i % 2), 80, ice,
            depth=26, finish="ice")
    foreground(cr, "snow")
    vignette(cr, a=0.28)

    if u < a0:
        host("point", hx, hy, 220)
    elif u <= a1:
        host("toss", hx, hy, 220, beat=k)
    else:
        host("toss", hx, hy, 220, beat=n + j)

stories.title: Flying Got This Much Safer In 20 Years

stories.question: Does flying make you nervous? Tell me why below.
stories.caption: Airline accidents per million flights fell from 3.72 in 2005 to 1.32 in 2025. The stat that actually matters: flying is roughly 190 times safer per mile than driving. Does flying make you nervous? Tell me why below. 👇

segments.say: Airlines averaged 3.72 accidents per million flights in 2005. By 2025 that fell to 1.32 — a third of what it was.
Fatal accidents dropped too: 1 in 3.5 million flights from 2012 to 2016, now 1 in 5.6 million — better systems catching failures first.
Per 100 million miles traveled, flying is roughly 190 times safer than driving. Per mile, your car is by far the riskier ride.

# scene standard: 2026-10-11
def _ar_line(cr, xr, yb, w, seed, ink, sz):
    # one line of Arabic handwriting, written right to left: a joined baseline
    # with teeth, tall alifs, a curl at each word's end, dots above and below
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(ink))
    cr.set_line_width(max(2.6, 0.2 * sz))
    cr.set_line_cap(cairo.LINE_CAP_ROUND)
    cr.set_line_join(cairo.LINE_JOIN_ROUND)
    x = xr
    i = 0
    while x > xr - w + 24:
        ww = 38 + ((seed * 7 + i * 13) % 5) * 15
        x0 = max(xr - w, x - ww)
        cr.move_to(x, yb)
        n = int((x - x0) / 10)
        for j in range(n):
            xx = x - j * 10
            cr.line_to(xx - 4, yb)
            if (seed + i + j) % 3 == 0:
                cr.line_to(xx - 6, yb - 0.4 * sz)
                cr.line_to(xx - 8, yb)
        cr.line_to(x0, yb)
        cr.curve_to(x0 - 7, yb + 2, x0 - 7, yb + 0.45 * sz, x0 + 3, yb + 0.45 * sz)
        cr.stroke()
        if (seed + i) % 2 == 0:
            cr.move_to(x - 4, yb)
            cr.line_to(x - 4, yb - 0.75 * sz)
            cr.stroke()
        for d in range((seed + i) % 3):
            dy = yb - 0.5 * sz if (i + d) % 2 else yb + 0.32 * sz
            cr.arc(x - 14 - d * 9, dy, max(1.6, 0.11 * sz), 0, 2 * math.pi)
            cr.fill()
        x = x0 - 16
        i += 1


def _en_line(cr, xl, yb, w, seed, ink, sz):
    # one line of Latin type, left to right: words as x-height blocks with
    # the odd ascender
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(ink))
    x = xl
    i = 0
    while x < xl + w - 24:
        ww = min(xl + w - x, 26 + ((seed * 5 + i * 11) % 6) * 12)
        cr.rectangle(x, yb - 0.42 * sz, ww, 0.42 * sz)
        cr.fill()
        if (seed + i) % 2 == 0:
            cr.rectangle(x, yb - 0.72 * sz, 5, 0.72 * sz)
            cr.fill()
        x += ww + 12
        i += 1


def _dome(cr, x, base, w, h, rgb):
    # a mosque on the skyline: a drum, a dome, a finial
    box(cr, x - w / 2, base, w, h, (214, 196, 168), depth=0.18 * w)
    cr.arc(x, base - h, w * 0.42, math.pi, 2 * math.pi)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, rgb, finish="gloss")
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((120, 100, 60)))
    cr.set_line_width(max(3, w * 0.012))
    cr.move_to(x, base - h - w * 0.42)
    cr.line_to(x, base - h - w * 0.42 - max(26, w * 0.09))
    cr.stroke()


def _minaret(cr, x, base, h):
    cylinder(cr, x - 16, base, 32, h, (222, 206, 178))
    for fr in (0.45, 0.78):
        cr.rectangle(x - 26, base - h * fr, 52, 12)
        solid(cr, (190, 174, 146), rim=False)
    cr.move_to(x - 16, base - h)
    cr.line_to(x, base - h - 52)
    cr.line_to(x + 16, base - h)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (90, 130, 120))


def _lantern(cr, x, base, s, t):
    # a brass fanous right by the camera: ring, pointed cap, three glass
    # panes of its six-sided body, a flame glowing inside
    glow(cr, x, base - 150 * s, 200 * s, (255, 190, 110), 0.35 + 0.05 * math.sin(t * 3))
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((150, 112, 50)))
    cr.set_line_width(6 * s)
    cr.arc(x, base - 330 * s, 18 * s, 0, 2 * math.pi)
    cr.stroke()
    cr.move_to(x - 70 * s, base - 250 * s)
    cr.line_to(x, base - 312 * s)
    cr.line_to(x + 70 * s, base - 250 * s)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, P["brass"], finish="metal")
    box(cr, x - 76 * s, base - 236 * s, 152 * s, 16 * s, P["brass"], depth=14 * s, finish="metal")
    panes = [(-70, -36, (224, 150, 70)), (-36, 36, (240, 196, 110)), (36, 70, (70, 150, 150))]
    for a_, b_, col in panes:
        cr.move_to(x + a_ * s, base - 236 * s)
        cr.line_to(x + b_ * s, base - 236 * s)
        cr.line_to(x + b_ * 0.86 * s, base - 50 * s)
        cr.line_to(x + a_ * 0.86 * s, base - 50 * s)
        cr.close_path()
        solid(cr, col, finish="glass", a=0.92)
    glow(cr, x, base - 140 * s, 46 * s, (255, 236, 170), 0.9)
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(P["brass_shade"]))
    cr.set_line_width(5 * s)
    for xx in (-36, 36):
        cr.move_to(x + xx * s, base - 236 * s)
        cr.line_to(x + xx * 0.86 * s, base - 50 * s)
    cr.stroke()
    box(cr, x - 66 * s, base, 132 * s, 50 * s, P["brass"], depth=14 * s, finish="metal")


def scene(cr, t, u, pts, host):
    """HERO: a laptop screen filling with Arabic writing
    SUBSTANCE: lines of Arabic script
    CAUSE: Data hammers the laptop's keys and every strike writes more lines of Arabic onto the screen
    A rooftop café at sunset over an Arabic city: a great golden dome and two
    minarets fading into the haze, a wooden table running back toward the
    parapet, and on it a laptop turned hard toward the sun, its screen
    receding into the picture, two pages open: English left, Arabic right.
    Ten years ago each page held ONE line; that line stays boxed as a dashed
    ghost with the old level marked across both. Data walks the keyboard
    hammering key after key, and every strike writes lines onto both pages
    at their real multiples: English creeps to under four lines while the
    Arabic page fills top to bottom, twenty-six times its old self. Done by
    0.66 and held; the cursor blinks, the tea steams, the lantern flickers,
    birds cross the sky, Data keeps hammering. By the camera: a brass
    lantern, a phone already written in Arabic, a glass of tea."""
    rows = [(str(l), float(v)) for l, v in pts]
    ar = next((r for r in rows if "arab" in r[0].lower()), max(rows, key=lambda r: r[1]))
    en = next((r for r in rows if "engl" in r[0].lower()), min(rows, key=lambda r: r[1]))
    rA = 1.0 + ar[1] / 100.0
    rE = 1.0 + en[1] / 100.0

    S = 6
    a0, a1 = 0.08, 0.66
    span = (a1 - a0) / S
    k = int(clamp((u - a0) / span, 0, S - 0.001))
    f = clamp((u - a0 - k * span) / span)
    g = ease(seg(f, 0.3, 0.85))                 # the lines write on the strike
    step = 0.0 if u < a0 else (k + g) / S
    done = u >= a0 and k == S - 1 and g >= 0.999
    LA = 1.0 + (rA - 1.0) * step
    LE = 1.0 + (rE - 1.0) * step

    # THE SETTING: an Arabic city at sunset, seen from a rooftop
    gy = landscape(cr, t, "town", horizon=1100)
    _dome(cr, 560, gy + 20, 560, 220, (206, 168, 84))          # the great mosque
    for x, w, h, col in ((20, 220, 110, (70, 132, 140)), (1070, 220, 120, (196, 160, 80))):
        _dome(cr, x, gy + 20, w, h, col)
    for x, h in ((80, 520), (1000, 560)):
        _minaret(cr, x, gy + 20, h)
    birds(cr, t, y0=680, n=5, rgb=(60, 50, 60))
    haze(cr, 560, 1140, (236, 196, 160), a=0.45)
    # the rooftop terrace: warm tiles running back to the parapet
    cr.move_to(0, 1150)
    cr.line_to(W, 1120)
    cr.line_to(W, H)
    cr.line_to(0, H)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (196, 150, 112), edge=False)
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((150, 108, 78), 0.5))
    cr.set_line_width(3)
    for i in range(12):
        cr.move_to(1300, 1060)
        cr.line_to(-1000 + i * 260, H)
    cr.stroke()
    box(cr, 0, 1180, W, 54, (214, 180, 140), depth=24)       # parapet

    # the table: its top running back into the picture, its front edge near
    cast_shadow(cr, 0, W, 1720, length=200, a=0.3)
    cr.move_to(70, 1330)
    cr.line_to(1080, 1290)
    cr.line_to(1080, 1690)
    cr.line_to(-20, 1690)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (150, 98, 62), finish="gloss")
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((110, 70, 44), 0.5))
    cr.set_line_width(3)
    for i in range(6):
        y_ = 1350 + i * 60
        cr.move_to(0, y_ + 10)
        cr.line_to(W, y_ - 30 + i * 6)
    cr.stroke()
    cr.rectangle(-20, 1690, W + 40, 40)
    solid(cr, (104, 66, 40), rim=False)

    # the laptop, turned hard toward the sun: its right side recedes
    SH, OX, BY, SC = -0.15, 560.0, 1560.0, 0.8

    def mp(x, y):
        return (OX + SC * (x - OX), BY + SC * (y - BY) + SH * SC * (x - OX))

    def kx(i):
        return 210 + 110 * i
    if u < a0:
        hx = kx(0)
    elif done or u >= a1:
        hx = kx(S - 1)
    else:
        hx = kx(k - 1 + ease(seg(f, 0.0, 0.25))) if k > 0 else kx(0)
    FOOT = 1432
    hit_x = hx + 75
    striking = a0 <= u < a1 and 0.3 <= f < 0.55

    lx0, ly0 = mp(40, 1460)
    lx1, ly1 = mp(1040, 1460)
    cast_shadow(cr, lx0, lx1, ly0, length=240, a=0.32)
    contact_shadow(cr, (lx0 + lx1) / 2, (ly0 + ly1) / 2 + 6, lx1 - lx0, a=0.5)

    cr.save()
    cr.transform(cairo.Matrix(SC, SH * SC, 0.0, SC, OX * (1 - SC),
                              BY * (1 - SC) - SH * SC * OX))
    # the laptop base and its keys
    cr.move_to(90, 1250)
    cr.line_to(990, 1250)
    cr.line_to(1040, 1440)
    cr.line_to(40, 1440)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (176, 180, 188), finish="metal")
    cr.rectangle(40, 1440, 1000, 20)
    solid(cr, (118, 122, 132), finish="metal", rim=False)
    for r_ in range(4):
        yb = 1286 + r_ * 44
        s_ = (yb - 1250) / 190.0
        xl, xr = 90 - 50 * s_ + 16, 990 + 50 * s_ - 16
        kw = (xr - xl) / 13.0
        for c_ in range(13):
            x_ = xl + c_ * kw
            down = r_ == 3 and striking and x_ <= hit_x < x_ + kw
            box(cr, x_ + 3, yb + (6 if down else 0), kw - 12, 24 - (6 if down else 0),
                (60, 62, 70) if not down else (90, 94, 104), depth=8)
            if down:
                glow(cr, x_ + kw / 2, yb - 10, 50, (255, 236, 190), 0.5)

    # the lid, its side going back into the picture, and the screen
    box(cr, 80, 1250, 880, 600, (70, 74, 84), depth=90, finish="metal")
    vgrad(cr, [(0, (30, 34, 44)), (1, (20, 22, 30))], 674, 1226, 104, 936)
    TOP, BOT = 736, 1214
    U = (BOT - TOP - 6) / rA                    # one line = ten years ago
    panes = [(120, 508, (92, 96, 106), "ENGLISH"), (532, 920, P["accent2"], "ARABIC")]
    for x0, x1, bar, name in panes:
        vgrad(cr, [(0, (250, 248, 243)), (1, (230, 233, 238))], 730, BOT, x0, x1)
        cr.rectangle(x0, 688, x1 - x0, 40)
        solid(cr, bar, finish="gloss", rim=False)
        for d in range(3):
            disc(cr, x0 + 18 + d * 18, 708, 6, (236, 232, 224))
        text(cr, name, x1 - 14, 718, 28, look.INK, anchor="right", shadow=False)

    ink = (34, 36, 44)
    w = 388 - 28
    xr = 920 - 14
    cur = None
    for i in range(int(math.ceil(LA))):
        fr = clamp(LA - i)
        if fr <= 0:
            continue
        cr.save()
        cr.rectangle(xr - w * fr - 2, TOP + i * U - 3, w * fr + 6, U + 6)
        cr.clip()
        _ar_line(cr, xr, TOP + i * U + U * 0.62, w, i * 3 + 1, ink, U)
        cr.restore()
        cur = (xr - w * fr - 6, TOP + i * U)
    xl = 120 + 14
    for i in range(int(math.ceil(LE))):
        fr = clamp(LE - i)
        if fr <= 0:
            continue
        cr.save()
        cr.rectangle(xl - 2, TOP + i * U - 3, w * fr + 4, U + 6)
        cr.clip()
        _en_line(cr, xl, TOP + i * U + U * 0.7, w, i * 5 + 2, (70, 76, 90), U)
        cr.restore()
    if cur is not None and (math.sin(t * 6.0) > 0 or not done):
        cr.rectangle(cur[0], cur[1] + 1, 3, U - 2)
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(P["accent2"]))
        cr.fill()

    # THE SCALE on the pages: the one line each held ten years ago
    if u > 0.06:
        la = ease(seg(u, 0.06, 0.12))
        cr.rectangle(124, TOP - 2, 380, U + 2)
        ghost(cr, a=0.85)
        cr.rectangle(536, TOP - 2, 380, U + 2)
        ghost(cr, a=0.85)
        then_mark(cr, 124, 760, TOP + U, "10 yrs ago", a=la)
    # English's own growth, written on its own mostly-empty page
    ea = ease(seg(u, a1, a1 + 0.04)) if done else 0.0
    if ea > 0:
        text(cr, f"+{en[1]:,.0f}%", 314, BOT - 50, 76, (110, 116, 130),
             face="display", anchor="center", shadow=False, alpha=ea)
    glow(cr, 280, 780, 280, (255, 226, 190), 0.14)    # the sunset on the glass
    cr.restore()

    # right by the camera: a brass lantern, a phone in Arabic, a glass of tea
    contact_shadow(cr, 470, 1880, 380, a=0.35)
    cr.move_to(300, 1770)
    cr.line_to(610, 1746)
    cr.line_to(652, 1870)
    cr.line_to(332, 1898)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (36, 38, 46), finish="gloss")
    cr.save()
    cr.move_to(322, 1778)
    cr.line_to(598, 1758)
    cr.line_to(634, 1862)
    cr.line_to(348, 1884)
    cr.close_path()
    cr.clip()
    vgrad(cr, [(0, (246, 244, 238)), (1, (220, 224, 230))], 1750, 1890, 310, 650)
    for i in range(4):
        _ar_line(cr, 610 + i * 6, 1792 + i * 24, 250, i + 7, ink, 18)
    cr.restore()
    contact_shadow(cr, 120, 1910, 260, a=0.4)
    _lantern(cr, 120, 1900, 1.3, t)
    contact_shadow(cr, 900, 1880, 170, a=0.35)
    cr.move_to(845, 1700)
    cr.line_to(955, 1700)
    cr.line_to(938, 1880)
    cr.line_to(862, 1880)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (176, 82, 40), finish="glass", a=0.9)
    cr.save()
    cr.scale(1, 0.3)
    cr.arc(900, 1700 / 0.3, 55, 0, 2 * math.pi)
    cr.restore()
    solid(cr, (206, 110, 56), finish="gloss")
    steam(cr, 900, 1660, t, strength=1.3)
    vignette(cr, a=0.3)

    fx, fy = mp(hx, FOOT)
    if u < a0:
        host("point", fx, fy, 220)
    elif u < 0.92:
        host("hammer", fx, fy, 220, beat=k if u < a1 + 0.02 else S + int((u - a1) / 0.09))
    else:
        host("hold_up", fx, fy, 220)

    if done:
        fit_readout(cr, f"+{ar[1]:,.0f}%", f"{ar[0]} web content in ten years",

        fit_readout(cr, "The web", "written in its own languages · ten years",

stories.closing: One court case turned every couch into a sportsbook.
stories.question: Have you ever placed a legal sports bet? Tell me below.
stories.caption: One Supreme Court ruling in 2018 struck down the law banning sports betting outside Nevada. Six years later it's legal in 38 states, and Americans wagered $150 billion on it in 2024 alone. What's the wildest bet you've ever made? 🏈

segments.say: In 2017, only Nevada could legally take a sports bet. Then the Supreme Court struck down the law banning it everywhere else, and by 2024, 38 states had followed.
By 2024, Americans legally wagered $150 billion on sports in a single year -- up from just $13 billion the first full year after the ban fell.
That's 76% of the country, up from just 2% before the ruling. The line didn't level off. It just kept climbing.

segments.say: Back in 2006, just 16% of Americans had a tattoo. Since then that has doubled.

# scene standard: 2026-10-11
def _tat_capsule(cr, x0, y0, x1, y1, r):
    a = math.atan2(y1 - y0, x1 - x0)
    cr.new_path()
    cr.arc(x1, y1, r, a - math.pi / 2, a + math.pi / 2)
    cr.arc(x0, y0, r, a + math.pi / 2, a + 3 * math.pi / 2)
    cr.close_path()


def _tat_half(x):
    # half-thickness of the arm: a slim wrist swelling to the upper arm
    if x < 620:
        return 95 + 30 * ease(clamp((x - 280) / 340.0))
    return 125 + 22 * ease(clamp((x - 620) / 380.0))


def _tat_top(cy, x):
    return cy - _tat_half(x) - 6 * math.sin((x - 280) / 340.0 * math.pi)


def _tat_arm_path(cr, cy, x0, x1):
    cr.new_path()
    xs = [x0 + (x1 - x0) * i / 40.0 for i in range(41)]
    cr.move_to(xs[0], _tat_top(cy, xs[0]))
    for x in xs[1:]:
        cr.line_to(x, _tat_top(cy, x))
    for x in reversed(xs):
        cr.line_to(x, cy + _tat_half(x))
    cr.close_path()


def _tat_star(cr, x, y, r, rgb):
    cr.new_path()
    for i in range(10):
        rr = r if i % 2 == 0 else r * 0.45
        a = -math.pi / 2 + i * math.pi / 5
        if i == 0:
            cr.move_to(x + rr * math.cos(a), y + rr * math.sin(a))
        else:
            cr.line_to(x + rr * math.cos(a), y + rr * math.sin(a))
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, rgb)


def _tat_heart(cr, x, y, s, rgb):
    cr.new_path()
    cr.move_to(x, y + 26 * s)
    cr.curve_to(x - 44 * s, y - 4 * s, x - 22 * s, y - 38 * s, x, y - 14 * s)
    cr.curve_to(x + 22 * s, y - 38 * s, x + 44 * s, y - 4 * s, x, y + 26 * s)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, rgb)


def _tat_rose(cr, x, y, s, ink):
    cr.save()
    cr.translate(x - 30 * s, y + 18 * s)
    cr.scale(1.0, 0.5)
    cr.arc(0, 0, 22 * s, 0, 2 * math.pi)
    cr.restore()
    solid(cr, (62, 120, 72))
    disc(cr, x, y, 28 * s, (190, 38, 46), finish="gloss")
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(ink))
    cr.set_line_width(5 * s)
    cr.arc(x, y, 9 * s, 0, 1.6 * math.pi)
    cr.arc(x, y, 18 * s, 1.6 * math.pi, 3.0 * math.pi)
    cr.stroke()


def _tat_machine(cr, x, y, s, t, live):
    # a classic coil tattoo machine, needle down on the skin at (x, y):
    # the steel tip and knurled grip, two copper coils on the frame, the
    # armature bar across them, the spring and the brass contact screw
    STEEL, IRON, COPPER = (178, 182, 192), (52, 54, 62), (196, 112, 56)
    buzz = (3.0 * s * math.sin(t * 90)) if live else 0.0
    # the power cord, looping up out of frame
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((24, 24, 28)))
    cr.set_line_width(12 * s)
    cr.move_to(x - 172 * s, y - 440 * s)
    cr.curve_to(x - 260 * s, y - 640 * s, W - 40, y - 700 * s, W + 40, 300)
    cr.stroke()
    # the needle
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((220, 224, 232)))
    cr.set_line_width(5 * s)
    cr.move_to(x, y)
    cr.line_to(x, y - 50 * s + buzz)
    cr.stroke()
    if live:
        # a wet bead of black ink where the needle meets the skin
        glow(cr, x, y, 40 * s, (255, 236, 200), 0.5)
        disc(cr, x, y + 4 * s, 13 * s, (14, 14, 18), finish="gloss")
    # tip, grip and tube
    cylinder(cr, x - 14 * s, y - 36 * s, 28 * s, 90 * s, STEEL, finish="metal")
    cylinder(cr, x - 26 * s, y - 126 * s, 52 * s, 124 * s, IRON, finish="metal")
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((120, 124, 134)))
    cr.set_line_width(3 * s)
    for j in range(9):
        yy = y - 136 * s - j * 12 * s
        cr.move_to(x - 24 * s, yy)
        cr.line_to(x + 24 * s, yy)
    cr.stroke()
    cylinder(cr, x - 12 * s, y - 250 * s, 24 * s, 70 * s, STEEL, finish="metal")
    # the frame: base plate and upright with its top arm
    box(cr, x - 185 * s, y - 246 * s, 210 * s, 26 * s, IRON, depth=30 * s, finish="metal")
    cr.rectangle(x - 190 * s, y - 455 * s, 30 * s, 212 * s)
    solid(cr, IRON, finish="metal")
    cr.rectangle(x - 190 * s, y - 455 * s, 112 * s, 24 * s)
    solid(cr, IRON, finish="metal")
    # the two copper coils with black caps
    for cx_ in (x - 150 * s, x - 88 * s):
        cylinder(cr, cx_, y - 272 * s, 54 * s, 118 * s, COPPER, finish="metal")
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((120, 60, 30), 0.8))
        cr.set_line_width(2.5 * s)
        for j in range(8):
            yy = y - 282 * s - j * 13 * s
            cr.move_to(cx_ + 2 * s, yy)
            cr.line_to(cx_ + 52 * s, yy)
        cr.stroke()
        box(cr, cx_ - 4 * s, y - 390 * s, 62 * s, 10 * s, (30, 30, 34), depth=12 * s)
    # the armature bar across the coils to the tube, buzzing
    cr.rectangle(x - 156 * s, y - 418 * s + buzz, 168 * s, 18 * s)
    solid(cr, STEEL, finish="metal")
    # the spring back to the frame
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((200, 204, 212)))
    cr.set_line_width(4 * s)
    cr.move_to(x - 160 * s, y - 412 * s + buzz)
    for j in range(5):
        cr.line_to(x - 168 * s - j * 3 * s, y - 418 * s - (j % 2) * 8 * s + buzz)
    cr.stroke()
    # the brass contact screw over the armature
    cylinder(cr, x - 108 * s, y - 418 * s, 16 * s, 22 * s, P["brass"], finish="metal")
    disc(cr, x - 100 * s, y - 443 * s, 14 * s, P["brass"], finish="metal")


def _tat_ink_bottle(cr, x, y, s, rgb, label):
    # a squat ink bottle with a nozzle cap and a paper label
    contact_shadow(cr, x + 30 * s, y, 80 * s, a=0.4)
    cylinder(cr, x, y, 60 * s, 90 * s, rgb, finish="gloss")
    cr.rectangle(x + 6 * s, y - 70 * s, 48 * s, 36 * s)
    solid(cr, (236, 228, 206), rim=False)
    cr.rectangle(x + 14 * s, y - 60 * s, 32 * s, 14 * s)
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(label))
    cr.fill()
    cylinder(cr, x + 18 * s, y - 88 * s, 24 * s, 22 * s, (30, 30, 34), finish="gloss")
    cylinder(cr, x + 26 * s, y - 108 * s, 8 * s, 22 * s, (240, 240, 244))


def scene(cr, t, u, pts, host):
    """HERO: an arm under a tattoo machine
    SUBSTANCE: black tattoo ink
    CAUSE: Data shoves a giant buzzing tattoo machine down the arm and its needle inks the skin as it goes
    One huge arm lies across a tattoo parlor's armrest, hand and fingers on
    the left, the T-shirt sleeve on the right: the WHOLE arm is all
    Americans. A coil tattoo machine as big as Data — copper coils, knurled
    grip, needle on the skin, cord looping up — stands on the arm. Each year
    Data shoves it down the arm from the sleeve, and behind the needle the
    skin turns solid wet BLACK INK — a blackwork sleeve, black with thin
    lines of bare skin showing through, a bead of ink at the needle — until
    that year's share of the arm is inked; the ink front is edged in the
    accent and every landed year leaves a notch under the arm. 2006's ink
    stays as a dashed box so the doubling reads at a glance. Done by 0.56
    and held; the fan keeps turning, the needle keeps buzzing and Data
    keeps shoving."""
    rows = by_time([(str(l), float(v)) for l, v in pts])
    n = len(rows)
    a0, a1 = 0.08, 0.56
    span = (a1 - a0) / max(1, n)
    k = int(clamp((u - a0) / span, 0, n - 0.001))
    f = clamp((u - a0 - k * span) / span)
    slide = ease(seg(f, 0.25, 0.65))           # the ink lands with the shove
    prev = rows[k - 1][1] if k > 0 else 0.0
    share = 0.0 if u < a0 else clamp((prev + (rows[k][1] - prev) * slide) / 100.0)
    landed_to = k if slide >= 0.999 else k - 1
    keep = sorted({round(i * (n - 1) / max(1, READOUT_SHOWS - 1))
                   for i in range(READOUT_SHOWS)}) if n > READOUT_SHOWS else list(range(n))
    named = max((i for i in keep if i <= landed_to), default=None)
    shown = None if (u < a0 or named is None) else rows[named]

    # the arm is drawn in its own coordinates and scaled up into the frame
    CY = 1060
    WX, SX = 280, 1000
    L = SX - WX
    S, OX, OY = 1.15, -120.0, -39.0
    INKC = (16, 16, 22)
    SKIN = (226, 178, 144)
    GOLD = (226, 178, 58)
    FLOOR = 1420

    def wx(x):
        return OX + S * x

    def wy(y):
        return OY + S * y

    def xat(v):
        return SX - L * v / 100.0

    def top_w(xw):
        xl = (xw - OX) / S
        return wy(_tat_top(CY, xl))

    def bot_w(xl):
        return wy(CY + _tat_half(xl))

    front = SX - L * share
    front_w = wx(front)

    # the parlor: a pale ceiling, a deep teal wall
    vgrad(cr, [(0, (200, 194, 180)), (1, (168, 160, 146))], 0, 250)
    vgrad(cr, [(0, (44, 76, 82)), (1, (24, 40, 46))], 250, FLOOR)
    cr.rectangle(0, 244, W, 12)
    solid(cr, (120, 96, 70), rim=False)
    # a wall of flash art, sheets pinned edge to edge
    for i, fx in enumerate((50, 255, 460, 665, 870)):
        fy = 650 + (i % 2) * 18
        cr.rectangle(fx, fy, 165, 215)
        solid(cr, (236, 226, 200))
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((60, 40, 30)))
        cr.set_line_width(8)
        cr.rectangle(fx, fy, 165, 215)
        cr.stroke()
        disc(cr, fx + 82, fy + 12, 7, (190, 40, 48), finish="gloss")
        kind = i % 3
        if kind == 0:
            _tat_heart(cr, fx + 82, fy + 115, 1.5, (190, 40, 48))
        elif kind == 1:
            _tat_star(cr, fx + 82, fy + 112, 56, GOLD)
        else:
            _tat_rose(cr, fx + 88, fy + 110, 1.4, INKC)
    # the neon sign
    glow(cr, 830, 310, 260, P["accent2"], 0.35)
    text(cr, "TATTOO", 830, 340, 78, P["accent2"], face="display", anchor="center")
    haze(cr, 250, FLOOR, (44, 76, 82), a=0.22)

    # the ceiling fan, always turning
    FX, FYc = 480, 150
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((70, 60, 50)))
    cr.set_line_width(10)
    cr.move_to(FX, 0)
    cr.line_to(FX, FYc)
    cr.stroke()
    for i in range(4):
        a = t * 1.6 + i * math.pi / 2
        ca, sa = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
        px, py = -sa, ca
        tip = (FX + ca * 280, FYc + sa * 280 * 0.3)
        cr.new_path()
        cr.move_to(FX + px * 14, FYc + py * 14 * 0.3)
        cr.line_to(tip[0] + px * 40, tip[1] + py * 40 * 0.3)
        cr.line_to(tip[0] - px * 40, tip[1] - py * 40 * 0.3)
        cr.line_to(FX - px * 14, FYc - py * 14 * 0.3)
        cr.close_path()
        solid(cr, (110, 72, 44))
    disc(cr, FX, FYc, 30, (150, 140, 120), finish="metal")

    # a checker floor running to the camera
    vgrad(cr, [(0, (196, 190, 178)), (1, (232, 228, 218))], FLOOR, H)
    cr.save()
    cr.rectangle(0, FLOOR, W, H - FLOOR)
    cr.clip()
    rows_y = [FLOOR + (H - FLOOR) * (i / 6.0) ** 1.5 for i in range(7)]

    def fxp(j, y):
        return 540 + j * 170 * (y - 1150) / (H - 1150)
    for i in range(6):
        for j in range(-12, 12):
            if (i + j) % 2:
                continue
            y0, y1 = rows_y[i], rows_y[i + 1]
            cr.move_to(fxp(j, y0), y0)
            cr.line_to(fxp(j + 1, y0), y0)
            cr.line_to(fxp(j + 1, y1), y1)
            cr.line_to(fxp(j, y1), y1)
            cr.close_path()
            cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((30, 30, 34), 0.6))
            cr.fill()
    cr.restore()

    # the armrest: a padded bed on a chrome post
    cast_shadow(cr, 420, 640, 1690, length=260, a=0.28)
    contact_shadow(cr, 530, 1690, 280, a=0.45)
    cr.save()
    cr.translate(530, 1686)
    cr.scale(1, 0.25)
    cr.arc(0, 0, 125, 0, 2 * math.pi)
    cr.restore()
    solid(cr, (60, 62, 68), finish="metal")
    cylinder(cr, 512, 1680, 36, 320, (186, 190, 198), finish="metal")
    box(cr, 240, 1400, 520, 64, (34, 34, 40), depth=70, finish="gloss")

    # a work light over the arm, warm on the skin
    glow(cr, front_w, top_w(front_w) + 80, 360, (255, 232, 190), 0.28)

    cr.save()
    cr.translate(OX, OY)
    cr.scale(S, S)
    # the hand: four fingers fanned, a thumb, the palm over their roots
    for i, (dy, ln) in enumerate(((-58, 130), (-20, 150), (18, 145), (54, 120))):
        _tat_capsule(cr, 230, CY + dy * 0.8, 230 - ln, CY + dy * 1.15, 24 - (i == 3) * 3)
        solid(cr, SKIN)
    _tat_capsule(cr, 260, CY - 70, 170, CY - 130, 26)
    solid(cr, SKIN)
    cr.save()
    cr.translate(250, CY)
    cr.scale(1.0, 0.95)
    cr.arc(0, 0, 90, 0, 2 * math.pi)
    cr.restore()
    solid(cr, SKIN)
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((150, 100, 80), 0.8))
    cr.set_line_width(4)
    for dy in (-46, -14, 18, 48):                   # knuckle creases
        cr.move_to(180, CY + dy - 8)
        cr.curve_to(170, CY + dy, 172, CY + dy + 6, 182, CY + dy + 12)
    cr.stroke()

    # the arm itself
    _tat_arm_path(cr, CY, WX, SX + 60)
    solid(cr, SKIN)

    # the ink: solid wet black ink, a blackwork sleeve from the shirt to the needle
    if share > 0.002:
        cr.save()
        _tat_arm_path(cr, CY, WX, SX + 60)
        cr.clip()
        cr.rectangle(front, 0, 2000, 3000)
        cr.clip()
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(INKC, 0.94))
        cr.paint()
        # thin lines of bare skin left showing through the black
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(SKIN, 0.55))
        cr.set_line_width(5)
        for j in range(14):
            xb = SX + 30 - j * 56
            h_ = _tat_half(xb)
            cr.move_to(xb, CY - h_ - 10)
            cr.curve_to(xb - 46, CY - 40, xb + 34, CY + 40, xb - 24, CY + h_ + 10)
        cr.stroke()
        # the fresh ink is WET: a glossy sheen along the lit top of the arm
        xs_ = [front + (SX + 60 - front) * i / 20.0 for i in range(21)]
        cr.new_path()
        cr.move_to(xs_[0], _tat_top(CY, xs_[0]) + 18)
        for x_ in xs_[1:]:
            cr.line_to(x_, _tat_top(CY, x_) + 18)
        for x_ in reversed(xs_):
            cr.line_to(x_, _tat_top(CY, x_) + 46)
        cr.close_path()
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((200, 206, 226), 0.28))
        cr.fill()
        cr.restore()
        # the share's edge, in the accent
        h_ = _tat_half(front)
        cr.set_source_rgba(*_c(P["accent2"]))
        cr.set_line_width(7)
        cr.move_to(front, CY - h_ - 16)
        cr.line_to(front, CY + h_ + 16)
        cr.stroke()
    _tat_arm_path(cr, CY, WX, SX + 60)
    edge(cr, (90, 56, 44))

    # the T-shirt sleeve the arm comes out of
    cr.new_path()
    cr.move_to(985, CY - 175)
    cr.line_to(1200, CY - 200)
    cr.line_to(1200, CY + 200)
    cr.line_to(975, CY + 175)
    cr.curve_to(960, CY + 60, 960, CY - 60, 985, CY - 175)
    cr.close_path()
    solid(cr, (150, 156, 168))
    cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((110, 114, 126)))
    cr.set_line_width(6)
    cr.move_to(1000, CY - 172)
    cr.curve_to(984, CY - 60, 984, CY + 60, 992, CY + 172)
    cr.stroke()
    cr.restore()

    # THE SCALE on the arm: 2006's ink as a dashed box, a notch per year
    if u >= a0:
        if landed_to >= 1:
            x06 = xat(rows[0][1])
            h6 = _tat_half(x06) * S
            cr.rectangle(wx(x06), wy(CY) - h6 - 22, wx(SX) - wx(x06), 2 * h6 + 44)
            ghost(cr, a=0.9)
        nxn = wx(xat(rows[named][1])) if named is not None else None
        for j in range(0, landed_to + 1):
            xl = xat(rows[j][1])
            nx = wx(xl)
            yb = bot_w(xl)
            cr.set_source_rgba(*_c((244, 238, 226)))
            cr.set_line_width(6)
            cr.move_to(nx, yb + 26)
            cr.line_to(nx, yb + 62)
            cr.stroke()
            if j == named or (j == 0 and nxn is not None and abs(nxn - nx) > 100):
                text(cr, rows[j][0], nx, yb + 104, 36, look.INK, face="bold",
                     anchor="center")

    # the tattoo machine itself, needle down on the ink front
    mx = min(front_w, 1010)
    _tat_machine(cr, mx, top_w(mx) + 4, 0.85, t, u >= a0)

    # right by the camera: the artist's steel tray of black ink bottles and caps
    contact_shadow(cr, 790, 1830, 560, a=0.45)
    box(cr, 520, 1820, 540, 34, (176, 180, 188), depth=90, finish="metal")
    for i in range(4):
        _tat_ink_bottle(cr, 560 + i * 92, 1792, 1.05, INKC, (20, 20, 24))
    cylinder(cr, 940, 1792, 90, 150, (240, 238, 232))
    for i in range(3):
        cylinder(cr, 70 + i * 70, 1880, 48, 34, INKC, finish="gloss")
    vignette(cr, a=0.28)

    # Data stands on the arm behind the machine and shoves it down the arm
    if u < a0:
        sx0 = 640
        host("point", sx0, top_w(sx0) + 6, 220)
    else:
        hx = min(mx + 80, 1000)
        hy = top_w(hx) + 6
        if u < a1 + 0.04:
            host("shove", hx, hy, 220, beat=k)
        else:
            host("shove", hx, hy, 220, beat=100 + int((u - a1) / 0.1))

    if shown is not None:
        lab, v = shown
        fit_readout(cr, f"{int(round(v))}%", f"of Americans have a tattoo · {lab}",
                    80, 520, a=ease(seg(u, a0, a0 + 0.05)), size=130)
    else:

segments.say: Tinder's US users sank to about 11 million in two years. Millions of people simply stopped swiping on the app everyone knows.

stories.title: For 70 Years, Fusion Lost Energy. Not Anymore.
stories.hook: One laser shot finally changed the math.
stories.closing: The hardest part of fusion just got easier. The rest is just engineering.
stories.question: Do you think fusion power arrives in your lifetime? Tell me below.

segments.topic: the fusion energy input vs output
segments.say: In 2022, a lab fired 2.05 megajoules of laser energy into a fuel pellet and got 3.15 back. For the first time ever, fusion produced more energy than it consumed.

segments.topic: how fusion energy output kept climbing
segments.say: It wasn't a one-off. By 2023 the same lab pushed the yield to 3.88 megajoules from a similar energy input, and repeated a net gain again in 2024.

segments.topic: the future of fusion energy power
segments.say: That energy only ran the lab's own lasers for a fraction of a second — a real power plant is still decades away. But the physics finally works, and that's the hard part.

stories.title: The World Made 62 Million Tons Of E-Waste
stories.hook: Your dead phone joined 62 million tons of trash, and the pile is growing fast.
stories.closing: One recycling bin at a time isn't going to cut it.
stories.question: How many old phones do you have sitting in a drawer right now? Tell me below.

segments.say: In 2022 the world produced 62 million tons of electronic waste, up 82 percent since 2010. That's enough to fill over a million and a half garbage trucks.

segments.topic: how much e-waste actually gets recycled
segments.say: Only 22 percent of it was properly collected and recycled. The other 78 percent got dumped, burned, or shipped off with no tracking at all.

segments.topic: the real cost of wasted e-waste materials
segments.say: That waste stream carries gold, copper, and rare earths, but recycling meets just 1 percent of global rare earth demand. We're throwing away a mine and digging a new one instead.

stories.hook_was: Only 1 in 5 of those tons get recycled.

stories.title: 51% Of The Internet Is Now Bots
stories.hook: More than half the web is bots now.
stories.closing: Half the internet you're scrolling might not even be watching itself.
stories.question: Does knowing that change how you use the internet? Tell me below.

segments.topic: how much internet traffic is bots
segments.say: In 2024, automated bot traffic hit 51 percent of all web traffic, finally passing humans for the first time in a decade.

segments.topic: bad bots vs good bots online
segments.say: Not all of it is harmless. 37 percent of all web traffic is now flagged as bad — scrapers, fake accounts, fraud — while only 14 percent are the good kind, like search crawlers.
And the malicious kind is growing faster than the rest — bad-bot traffic alone climbed from 30 percent in 2022 to 37 percent in 2024, as AI makes bots cheaper to build than ever.

stories.title: Brain Plastic Levels Rose 50% Since 2016
stories.hook: Your brain may hold a spoon's worth of plastic.
stories.closing: And that number's still climbing.
stories.question: Does that change how you think about plastic packaging? Tell me below.

segments.topic: how much plastic is in the brain
segments.say: A 2024 study found human brain tissue holds about 4,900 micrograms of micro and nanoplastics per gram, up nearly 50 percent from 3,345 in 2016 samples.

segments.topic: where all that brain plastic comes from
segments.say: It's not mysterious. The average person swallows about 5 grams of microplastic a week — roughly a credit card's worth — through food, water, and indoor air.

segments.topic: what plastic in the brain actually does
segments.say: Scientists don't know if plastic causes dementia, but brains with a dementia diagnosis carry three to five times more of it than brains without one — a link worth watching, not yet an answer.

stories.title: Why New Cars All Look The Same Color Now
stories.hook: 80% of new cars are white, black, or gray.
stories.closing: Somewhere, a bright yellow car is very lonely.
stories.question: What color is your car? Tell me it isn't gray.
stories.caption: 80% of new cars sold today are white, black, gray, or silver, up from 60% in 2004. Red and green combined? Down to just 9.2%. What color is your car? 👇

segments.topic: why new cars all look the same color
segments.say: By 2023, 80 percent of new cars sold in America were white, black, gray, or silver. Back in 2004, grayscale colors were only 60 percent of the market. Color is quietly disappearing from the road.

segments.topic: which colors new cars actually come in now
segments.say: White leads at 27.6 percent, black at 22, gray at 21.3, and silver at 9.1. Add them up and grayscale is basically the entire market.
Red and green used to be real choices. In 1996 they made up 33.5 percent of new cars combined. By 2025, that's down to 9.2 percent. Color didn't fade, buyers just stopped choosing it.

stories.title: All The Gold Ever Mined Fits In A 22-Meter Cube
stories.hook: 216,000 tons of gold. One tiny cube.
stories.closing: Turns out humanity's greed fits in a hotel lobby.
stories.question: Would you even recognize that much gold if you saw it? Guess below.
stories.caption: By 2024, humanity had mined 216,000 tonnes of gold, enough to melt into a cube just 22.3 meters wide. Nearly half of it became jewelry. Would you recognize that much gold if you saw it? 👇

segments.topic: how much gold humanity has ever mined
segments.say: Every ounce of gold ever mined is still sitting somewhere. By 2024 the stockpile hit 216 thousand tonnes, and most came out of the ground in just the last 70 years.

segments.topic: where all that mined gold actually sits
segments.say: So where did it go? 45 percent became jewelry. Another 22 percent sits in bars, coins, and ETFs. And 17 percent is locked in central bank vaults, doing nothing but existing.

segments.topic: how big the melted gold cube really is
segments.say: Melt every bit of it into one cube and it's only 22.3 meters a side, less than half the length of an Olympic pool. All that mining, and it barely fills a hotel lobby.

stories.title: 1 In 3 Couples Now Sleep In Separate Rooms
stories.hook: Sleeping apart isn't the red flag you think.
stories.closing: Turns out the honeymoon phase has quiet hours.
stories.question: Do you and your partner still sleep in the same room? Tell me below.
stories.caption: 1 in 3 couples now sleep in separate rooms, and Millennials do it twice as often as Boomers. The #1 reason, by far: snoring. Do you and your partner still share a bed? 👇

segments.topic: how many couples are sleeping apart
segments.say: Every year since 2023, the American Academy of Sleep Medicine has asked. The answer keeps landing around a third: 35 percent in 2023, 29 in 2024, 33 again in 2025. This isn't a phase.

segments.topic: which couples sleep apart the most
segments.say: It's not evenly spread. 43 percent of Millennial couples say they sleep separately. Only 22 percent of Boomers do. The generation raised on personal space is applying it to marriage.

segments.topic: why couples actually end up in separate rooms
segments.say: The number one reason, by far: snoring, 52 percent blame it. Phone scrolling and nighttime bathroom trips tie for second, 33 percent each. Love doesn't fix bad sleep hygiene.

stories.title: Coffee Just Hit $4.41 A Pound — A Record
stories.hook: Your coffee habit is about to get pricier.
stories.closing: Drink it slow. It earned that price.
stories.question: Have you noticed your coffee getting more expensive? Tell me below.
stories.caption: Arabica coffee futures hit a record $4.41 a pound in February 2025, more than double what it cost a year earlier. Brazil's drought is the reason. Have you noticed your coffee bill creeping up? 👇

segments.topic: how high coffee prices have climbed
segments.say: Arabica coffee futures hit $4.41 a pound in February 2025, the highest price ever recorded. Back in 2019 it was around $1.05. The climb wasn't steady, it was a series of shocks.
The shock is Brazil's drought. One trade house cut its Brazil arabica forecast from 45.4 million bags to just 34.4 million, an 11-million-bag hole in the world's biggest coffee supply overnight.

segments.topic: how much coffee prices have doubled
segments.say: That's why your cup costs more than it did a year ago. $2.00 a pound in February 2024. $4.41 by February 2025. More than double, in twelve months.

stories.title: 1 In 5 Americans Has Now Taken A Weight-Loss Shot
stories.hook: One drug rewired how America eats.
stories.closing: Ozempic didn't fix willpower. It just changed the math.
stories.caption: GLP-1 drug use in the US nearly doubled in a single year. These shots work far better than anything before them -- but half the people taking them say they can barely keep affording it. Here's the data behind the fastest-adopted drug class in a generation. What's your take?

segments.topic: how many Americans have taken the weight-loss shot
segments.say: By 2024, 12 percent of US adults had tried a weight-loss shot. One year later, 18 percent -- nearly 1 in 5.

segments.topic: why the weight-loss shot actually works
segments.say: Here's why: old diet pills took off maybe 5 percent of body weight. The newest weight-loss shot averages 21. That gap is the whole story.
But half of everyone taking the weight-loss shot says it's hard to keep affording it, even with insurance.

stories.question: Have you or anyone close to you tried one? Tell me below.

stories.title: Why Are 1 In 37 US Babies Now Born Via IVF?
stories.hook: It used to be almost unthinkable.
stories.closing: Science got better. The bill didn't get any smaller.
stories.caption: IVF's share of US births has grown fast, and success rates for younger patients are now near 50%. But one cycle still costs about as much as a used car -- and most people need more than one. Here's how fertility science outran affordability. Ever priced this out yourself?

segments.topic: how many US babies are born via IVF
segments.say: In 2013, IVF was behind about 1.5 percent of US babies. By 2022, it was 2.5 percent -- 1 in 37 births.
Here's why: live-birth success per cycle for women under 35 is now near 50 percent. Past 42, it drops to just 4.
One cycle runs about 20,000 dollars. Most patients need more than one -- so the real total is closer to 50,000.

stories.question: Would you consider IVF if you needed it? Say why below.

stories.title: Invasive Species Now Cost The World $423 Billion A Year
stories.hook: That's more than most countries make.
stories.closing: Nature sent the world a bill nobody budgeted for.
stories.caption: The global bill for invasive species has quadrupled every decade since 1970 -- it's now bigger than the economy of Norway. Most of that money isn't even spent stopping them; it's just cleaning up the damage. Here's where $423 billion a year actually goes. What's invaded your area?

segments.say: The global bill for invasive species has roughly quadrupled every decade since 1970 -- reaching 423 billion dollars a year.
Almost all of it, over 90 percent, pays for damage already done. Barely 10 percent goes to stopping the next invasion.

segments.topic: how many invasive species there really are
segments.say: Over 37 thousand alien species have taken hold worldwide. Only about 3.5 thousand of them are the ones actually causing the damage.

stories.question: Ever seen an invasive species mess up your own backyard? Tell me below.

Even though that number has since dropped to 6,288, the total lost since 1970 already tops 750,000 square kilometers -- bigger than France. Nearly 80% of it becomes cattle pasture. segments.say: In 2004 Brazil cleared 27,772 square kilometers of Amazon rainforest in one year. By 2024 that had fallen all the way to 6,288 -- the lowest in almost a decade.
But add up every year since 1970, and the Amazon has lost about 750,000 square kilometers total -- an area bigger than the whole country of France.
